structured_stats.description:
The '''Brawler''' is a hardcore melee tower that attacks enemies with its mechanical fists. It can be purchased from the store for {{Gem|1,250}} and has a level requirement of {{Level|50}}.

The '''Brawler''' attacks enemies with its mechanical fists, dealing damage. At Level 2, it gains the ability to combo its attacks, making it attack enemies in a burst of three continuous attacks, which ends in a cooldown. The burst does not restart if there are no more enemies in its range. For example, if it lands two hits on enemies and stops attacking, the next hit will be a final hit. The final hit from a combo will deal increased damage and knock back enemies. The enemy is not always pushed back the same distance, as this is determined by its size. Larger enemies will be pushed back less than an average-sized enemy. Knockback has a 3 second long cooldown before it can be applied again.

The '''Brawler''' also has a unique ability where it can change its current position into one which the player can select. However, this ability has a cooldown of thirty seconds. Upon landing, it will create a shockwave that deals a decent amount of damage to enemies and knocks them back. Uniquely, the ''Reposition'' ability can damage [[Flying]] enemies.

The '''Brawler''' is considered an all-round tower due to its cheap placement cost, good DPS, and ability to knockback enemies from Level 2+.

The '''Brawler''' has a placement limit of ten per player. This is decreased to six in [[PVP]] mode.

It had a decent amount of health and an above average speed. It has one ability, ''Distorted Reposition'', where it jumps from one path to another. If there is only one path, it will just slightly behind or in front of itself, landing on the same path. While jumping, it becomes a [[Flying]] enemy. Upon landing, it creates a shockwave with a radius of 15, which stuns towers hit by it for 3 seconds and deals 1,500 damage to units. This ability has a range of 30, meaning it will not be performed if the '''Null Brawler''' has no towers near it. ==Logbook Description== "''Brawler ducked under a right hook, slipped left, and drove an uppercut into its stomach. As the creature doubled over, landed a clean shot to its face. Brawler bounced on his toes, rolling his shoulders, and spat to the side. "Felt good, didn't it?" As the creature stood, Brawler could swear the thing was grinding back at him.''" ==Appearance== The '''Null Brawler''' is a corrupted recreation of the Level 5 [[Brawler]]. It has purple skin and hair, with parts of its body being covered in purple goo. It wears a red vest, blue overalls and black shoes. On its left arm, it has grey and orange mechanical fists, while on its right, it has purple fingers. ==Event Strategy== As this enemy only appears through [[Sandbox Mode|Sandbox]] mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. ==Description==
The '''Damage Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's damage, making them stronger. It is displayed on the tower itself with the icon of an arm with muscle.

==Mechanics==
'''Damage Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Damage × (1 + Damage Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Damage Buff''' is the debuff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The damage increased by the '''Damage Buff''' will always round down to the nearest integer. For example, a tower that deals 5 damage with a 50% '''Damage Buff''' will deal 7 damage, instead of 7.5.

Multiple towers are not fully affected by the buff. A full list of towers affected fully, partially or that are unaffected can be found below.
{{DamageBuff}}

==Applied By==
The following towers or consumables can apply the '''Damage Buff''' to other towers or itself:
*[[DJ Booth]] (Passive)
*[[Mercenary Base]] (Passive)
*[[Damage Flag]] (Passive)
*[[War Machine]] (Passive)
*[[Medic]] (''Ubercharge'' ability)
*[[Warden]] (When parrying)

The following event features can apply the '''Damage Buff''' to towers:

* [[Justice]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])
* [[The Chariot]] (Passive, [[Null & Void Event|Null & Void]])

The following towers used to have the '''Damage Buff''':
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Crook Boss]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Minigunner]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Pyromancer]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Scout]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Golden}} [[Cowboy]] (Passive)
*[[Militant|John]] (''Enraging Shout'' ability)
*[[Slasher|Shredder]] (''Knife Throw'' ability)
*[[Cowboy]] (''Wildest of the West and Gold Rush'' abilities'')''
*[[Gladiator]] (''Sharp Edge'' ability'')''

The following tower used to apply the '''Damage Buff''' to other towers:
*[[Militant|John]] (''Enraging Shout'' ability)

The following removed towers had the '''Damage Buff''':
*{{Color|Platinum}} [[Crook Boss]] (Passive)
*{{Color|Platinum}} [[Minigunner]] (Passive)

==Description==
The '''Range Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's range. It is shown on the tower with a blue icon of multiple waves.

==Mechanics==
'''Range Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Range × (1 + Range Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Range Buff''' is the buff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The range of a tower affected by the '''Range Buff''' can be in decimal form, instead of being rounded down or rounded up to the nearest interger. For example, a tower with 5 range with a 50% '''Range Buff''' will have a range of 7.5.

The following towers are either partially or fully not affected by the '''Range Buff''':
*All [[units]].
*The [[Shotgunner]], as its bullets do not extend into the increased range.
*The [[DJ Booth]] cannot have its range boosted by another [[DJ Booth]].
**Other range buff sources, like the [[Ranger]], can still apply it.
*Circling range of the [[Pursuit]] and [[Ace Pilot]].
**The radius in which towers gain hidden detection from the [[Ace Pilot]] also cannot be increased.
**These towers' attack range can still be increased.
*The sentry building range of the [[Engineer]].

related_pages.title: Damage Indicators
related_pages.wikitext_excerpt:
==Description==
'''Damage Indicators''' are numbers that pop up on enemies when a tower is selected. These numbers are how much damage was dealt to the enemy. The colors used by them mainly varies based on the damage type of the tower or unit. As not all damage types are registered by the game, not all sources of damage will have them appear.
__TOC__

==Regular Indicators==
[[File:RegularIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Regular indicators are the basic indicator that appears on most towers. These indicators are colored red. If a tower does not fall into any of the categories below, it uses these indicators.
{{Clear}}

==Explosion Indicators==
[[File:ExplosionIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Explosion indicators appear when a tower or unit deals explosion damage. They are also appear when a tower deals burn damage. These indicators are colored orange. Additionally, damage under this type will bypass defense. These following towers and units deal this type of damage:
*[[Demoman]]
*[[Ace Pilot]]
*[[Military Base]]
*[[Tank]]
*[[Railgun Tank]]
*[[Rocketeer]]
*[[Trapper]]
*[[Pyromancer]]
*[[Tesla]]
*[[Necromancer]]
*[[Archer]]
*[[Commando]]
*[[Firework Technician]]
*[[Jester]]
*[[Snowballer]]
*[[Swarmer]]
*[[Missile APC]]
*[[Grenadier]]
*[[War Machine Sentry]]
*[[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]]
*[[Gift Bomber]]
*[[Ripped Elf (Unit)|Ripped Elf]]

However, despite this, not every single explosive actually uses these indicators. The following towers do not use explosive indicators, meaning they do not bypass defense:
*[[Paintballer]]
**Uses Regular indicators.
*[[Slime Trooper]]
**Uses Regular indicators.
*[[Hallow Punk]]
**Uses Regular indicators.
*[[Ivy]]
**Uses Energy indicators.

Additionally, the [[Elementalist]] uses similarly colored damage indicators for its burn related attacks, though it shares no other traits with explosion indicators, such as defense bypass.

==Collision Indicators==
[[File:CollisionIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Collision indicators appear when a tower or unit deals unit collision damage. This means it has a few traits, such as bypassing defense, damaging [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies, bypassing [[Tank (Attribute)|Tank]]  and dealing no damage to [[Ghost (Attribute)|Ghost]] enemies. These indicators are colored yellow. This means it will mainly appear when a unit collides with another enemy. There is one exception to this, as the [[Trapper]]'s spike and bear traps deal unit collision damage, making them use these indicators.

==Melee Indicators==
[[File:MeleeIndicators.png|100px|thumb]]
Melee indicators appear when a tower or unit deals melee damage. These indicators are yellow. These indicators are quite inconsistent, as multiple towers that would be considered melee are not registered as ones. These following towers and units deal this type of damage:
*[[Gladiator]]
*[[Warden]]
*[[Sledger]]
*[[Executioner]]
*[[Riot Guard]]
*[[Slasher]]
**With its main attack.
*[[Assassin]]
*[[Warlock]]
**With its melee attack.
*[[Brawler]]
These towers, despite looking like they would deal such damage, do not have melee indicators:
*[[Sword Skeleton]] and [[Skeleton Knight]].
**Both use regular indicators.
*[[Executioner Skeleton]].
**Despite [[Executioner]] having melee indicators, [[Executioner Skeleton]] does not. It has regular indicators.
*[[Guardian Elf]]
**Uses regular indicators.

==Poison Indicators==
[[File:PoisonIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Poison indicators appear when a tower deals poison damage. These indicators are colored green. These following towers and units deal this type of damage:
*[[Toxic Gunner]]
*[[Saboteur]]
*[[Ivy]]
*[[Jester]]

The [[Swarmer]]'s sting damage used to have its damage create such indicators, though this is not longer the case starting from [[v1.63.0]].

==Chillness Indicators==
[[File:ChillnessIndicator.png|100px|thumb]]
Chillness indicators appear when a tower deals damage through chillness. These indicators are colored blue. While all freezing tower apply chillness, only the [[Cryomancer]

related_pages.title: Firerate Bug
related_pages.wikitext_excerpt:
{{Removed|date = 6th of June 2026}}
{{Improve|this page and majority of tower/unit pages require updating}}
The '''Firerate Bug''', also known as the '''RoF (Rate of Fire) Bug''', was a bug that slightly increased the firerate of all towers and units. This increase was not displayed on the statistics in the game. This bug significantly affected the statistics of fast-firing towers, such as the [[Minigunner]] and [[Ace Pilot]], by significantly decreasing their DPS, whereas slow-firing towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Sniper]] were hardly affected.

This has been fixed as of the 6th of June 2026, and all firerate statistics in the game are considered to be accurate unless affected by a different unrelated bug.

{{RightTOC}}

==Prior to 5th of June 2026==
The '''Firerate Bug''' affects all towers and units that can directly attack enemies, meaning the only towers that are not affected are the [[Farm]], [[Medic]] and the [[Firework Technician]] and the only units that are not affected are the [[Humvee]], [[Humvee 2]], [[Elf]], [[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]], [[Skeleton (Unit)|Skeleton]], [[Giant Skeleton (Unit)|Giant Skeleton]] and [[Hallow Guard (Unit)|Hallow Guard]]. The '''Firerate Bug''' does not affect the firerate of some secondary attacks towers or units may perform, some damage-over-time effects applied by towers (like burn from the [[Pyromancer]]) or certain other cooldowns.

The '''Firerate Bug''' increases the firerate of a tower/unit depending on its firerate, which can vary anywhere between 0.017 and 0.032 seconds. The firerate increase affects fast firing towers the most; for example, the [[Minigunner]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 0.09, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 0.117, decreasing its DPS from 166.67 to 128.20, which is a decrease of 38.47 DPS, or a loss of about 23.08 DPS. Meanwhile, slow firing towers are barely affected by it; for example, the [[Ranger]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 8, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 8.025, decreasing its DPS from 156.26 to 155.76, which is a decrease of 0.30 DPS, or a loss of 0.2% DPS.

The [[Firerate Buff]] is also affected by the '''Firerate Bug''', making it less effective. For example, the Level 4 [[Minigunner]] without the '''Firerate Bug''' with a 50% firerate boost should have a firerate of 0.06, but with the '''Firerate Bug''' it has a firerate of 0.083. This means that its DPS with a 50% firerate boost is decreased from 250 to 180.72, which is a decrease of 69.28 DPS, or a loss of 27.71% DPS.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units is increased by specific values based on the firerate. While technically possible to calculate by hand, due to the effort it would take, it is overall recommended to either use [[Help:Neowtext#ROFBUG|Neowtext]] or [https://fiheron.github.io/dps-calc/ an online calculator].

==Prior to the 9th of January 2023==
Prior to the 9th of January 2023, the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was higher than it currently is. The firerate increase was generally around 0.03 seconds. For towers, the firerate increase remained at around 0.008 seconds.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units after the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]] and before the 9th of January 2023 is increased by 0.008 and 0.03 respectively, unless stated otherwise. This does not, however, mean the actual value is this; it can vary between towers and even between matches.

==Prior to the Violent Night Update==
Prior to the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]], the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was lower than it was before the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]]. The firerate increases could be anywhere between 0.008 and 0.017 seconds, but the increase was generally around 0.008 seconds. This is the same as the current situation.

Towers need flying detection to target these enemies. ==Mechanics== '''Flying''' enemies fly above the path, which grants them multiple perks. The main immunity that it grants is requiring flying detection to target them, making it difficult for towers without said detection to damage a '''Flying''' enemy. '''Flying''' enemies have various other unique immunities that are applied, outside of flying detection: # They are completely immune to being damaged by unit collision damage, even if they would normally collide with each other. #*This includes the [[Gift Bomber]], which cannot collide with '''Flying''' enemies, despite visually passing through '''Flying''' enemies. #*Some units, like the [[Rifleman]] or [[Missile APC]], can detect flying enemies, even if they cannot collide with them. #They are able to fly over road hazards, namely the [[Trapper]]'s traps and the [[Harvester]]'s thorns (and by extension the [[Farm]]'s). #*The [[Commando]]'s missiles, can still affect them. #*The [[Barricade]] can collide with '''Flying''' enemies, but they deal unit collision damage. Therefore, '''Flying''' enemies are also immune to this. #They are immune to being knocked back by towers. This does not mean they are immune to other effects from attacks that knock back enemies. #*For example, the [[DJ Booth]] can still slow down '''Flying''' enemies, even if the purple track cannot knock them back. '''Flying''' enemies may be indirectly damaged by towers, even if they do not have flying detection. For example, the [[Brawler]]'s ''Reposition'' ability deals damage to '''Flying''' enemies, though due to their knockback immunity it does not knock them back. Build up chill to slow and freeze enemies in their tracks!|Store Description}} |-|Version 3 = {{QuoteBox|Chill enemies to a slow freeze!|Store Description}} |-|Version 2 = {{QuoteBox|Shoot an ice beam, freezing targets for a few seconds.|Store Description}} |-|Version 1 = {{QuoteBox|Freeze zombies temporarily with a freeze ray!|Former Store Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Freezer''' is a ground [[Towers|tower]] that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for {{Coins|650}}. The '''Freezer''' targets a single enemy and fires a ''Frost Ray'', chilling the enemy and slowing it down. The chillness slowness effect stacks with each hit multiple times. This chillness effect also deals damage over time, chipping away the health of enemies affected by it. Starting from Level 2, it can freeze enemies. When the chillness slowness effect is higher than the max slowdown, the enemy will be frozen, which generally when targeting a single enemy takes four or five shots. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with [[Freeze Immunity]] also cannot be frozen, slowed down or have their defense dropped by the '''Freezer'''. At Level 3+, the '''Freezer''' fires in bursts, with a short delay between them. Additionally, at Level 3+, it drops defense by 10% every tick. It can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%. On top of this, it will also start dealing damage over time with its chill at Level 3. Additionally at Level 4, the '''Freezer''' gains the ability to throw a '''Frost Grenade''', freezing enemies within an explosion radius. The '''Freezer''' does well as an all-rounder support tower. Due to its generally low price and decent DPS, the '''Freezer''' can be a solid choice for early-game defense to mid game with very good cost efficiency. Towards late game, the '''Freezer''' is useful for stalling, defense melting and deal additional DPS through its damage over time, though its DPS is insufficient to deal with late-game waves alone. The '''Freezer''' has [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] detection from Level 0 and [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] detection from level 2.
